# Clean Path Credit

> Bilingual (English / Spanish) credit repair and restoration company serving Texas — focused on San Antonio and Houston. Founded by Alex Serratos. Operates under the Credit Repair Organizations Act (CROA), the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA), and Texas Finance Code Chapter 393. No advance fees. 3-day right to cancel. No guaranteed outcomes. Contact: hello@cleanpathcredit.com · (346) 399-5606.

Clean Path Credit audits consumer credit reports across Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion, identifies items that appear inaccurate, incomplete, or unverifiable, and files disputes on the consumer's behalf under FCRA §611 (credit bureau disputes) and §623 (furnisher disputes). The company does not charge advance fees (prohibited by CROA §404), provides the Consumer Credit File Rights notice before any contract is signed, and honors a 3-day unconditional right to cancel (CROA §405). Services are delivered remotely (service-area business, by appointment) in English and Spanish.

## Key facts (quotable)
- Clean Path Credit is a Texas credit-services organization founded by Alex Serratos, serving San Antonio and all of Texas in English and Spanish.
- Under CROA §404, a credit repair company cannot legally charge fees before services are performed. Clean Path Credit bills per completed dispute round, never upfront.
- Under CROA §405, consumers have a 3-day right to cancel any credit repair contract at no cost.
- Under FCRA §611, a credit bureau must investigate a disputed item — generally within 30 days — and correct or delete anything it cannot verify.
- No legitimate company, including Clean Path Credit, can remove accurate, verifiable, and timely information or guarantee a specific credit score.
- In Texas, credit services organizations must register under Finance Code Chapter 393 and post a surety bond; consumers can verify registration with the Texas Office of Consumer Credit Commissioner (OCCC).

## Are credit repair companies legal?
Yes. In the United States, credit repair is regulated by the Credit Repair Organizations Act (CROA), which requires a written contract, prohibits charging fees before services are performed, mandates a 3-day right to cancel, and forbids guaranteed-outcome claims. The disputes a credit repair company files are the same rights consumers hold themselves under FCRA §611. A legitimate company cannot remove accurate, verifiable information or guarantee a specific credit score.

## How long does credit repair take?
There is no guaranteed timeline. By law (FCRA §611), credit bureaus generally have 30 days to investigate each disputed item, so the process works in dispute rounds rather than a fixed number of days. Results vary by individual circumstance, and no honest company can promise a specific score or date.
